claim: HEK293 cells endogenously express β2ARs
source: Human embryonic kidney (HEK293) cells comprise a well established model system for investigating GPCR signaling via the cAMP cascade, particularly signaling initiated by β2ARs which are endogenously expressed in these cells (Violin et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Violin et al., 2008

claim: β2AR stimulates cAMP production primarily from the plasma membrane in HEK293 cells
source: The β2AR stimulates cAMP production primarily from the plasma membrane, with endosomal activation contributing a relatively small but functionally significant fraction (Irannejad et al., 2013; Tsvetanova and von Zastrow, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior studies

claim: AC3 and AC6 are the most highly expressed AC isoforms in HEK293 cells
source: AC3 and AC6 are the most highly expressed AC isoforms and are major producers of global cAMP in these cells, while AC1 and AC9 transcripts are expressed at only moderately reduced levels and comparable to one another (Soto-Velasquez et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Soto-Velasquez et al., 2018

claim: AC1 and AC9 transcripts are expressed at comparable levels in HEK293 cells
source: AC3 and AC6 are the most highly expressed AC isoforms and are major producers of global cAMP in these cells, while AC1 and AC9 transcripts are expressed at only moderately reduced levels and comparable to one another (Soto-Velasquez et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Soto-Velasquez et al., 2018

claim: Flag-tagged AC1 tolerates an N-terminal Flag tag
source: We examined the subcellular localization of AC1 and AC9 using a recombinant epitope tagging strategy, beginning with AC1 because this isoform was shown previously to tolerate an N-terminal Flag tag (Chen et al., 1997).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chen et al., 1997

claim: Flag-AC1 localizes primarily to the plasma membrane in HEK293 cells
source: When expressed in HEK293 cells, Flag-tagged AC1 (Flag-AC1) localized primarily to the plasma membrane, similar to a co-expressed HA-tagged β2AR construct (HA-β2AR).
evidence: Directly stated observation from experiments

claim: Isoproterenol promotes HA-β2AR redistribution to cytoplasmic punctae within minutes
source: Application of the β-adrenergic agonist isoproterenol promoted HA-β2ARs to redistribute within minutes to cytoplasmic punctae, as described previously, but Flag-AC1 remained at the plasma membrane (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by experimental observation shown in Figure 1A

claim: Flag-AC1 remains at the plasma membrane after isoproterenol treatment
source: Application of the β-adrenergic agonist isoproterenol promoted HA-β2ARs to redistribute within minutes to cytoplasmic punctae, as described previously, but Flag-AC1 remained at the plasma membrane (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by experimental observation shown in Figure 1A

claim: Flag tagging does not disrupt the functional activity of AC9
source: We applied a similar tagging strategy to AC9 and verified that Flag tagging also does not disrupt the functional activity of AC9 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: Verified by experimental data shown in supplementary figures

claim: Flag-AC9 localizes predominantly in the plasma membrane in the absence of agonist
source: Flag-AC9 localized predominantly in the plasma membrane in the absence of agonist, similar to Flag-AC1.
evidence: Direct observation from experiments

claim: Flag-AC9 redistributes to intracellular punctae after isoproterenol application
source: However, after application of isoproterenol, Flag-AC9 redistributed to intracellular punctae, the majority of which also contain internalized HA-β2AR (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by experimental observation shown in Figure 1B

claim: The majority of Flag-AC9-containing punctae also contain internalized HA-β2AR
source: However, after application of isoproterenol, Flag-AC9 redistributed to intracellular punctae, the majority of which also contain internalized HA-β2AR (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by experimental observation shown in Figure 1B

claim: AC9-GFP redistributes to endosomes after isoproterenol treatment
source: AC9 labeled in its C-terminal cytoplasmic domain with GFP (AC9-GFP) also redistributed, enabling live-cell confocal imaging which revealed mobile AC9-containing endosomes (Video 1).
evidence: Supported by live-cell imaging data shown in Video 1

claim: AC9-containing endosomes are mobile
source: AC9 labeled in its C-terminal cytoplasmic domain with GFP (AC9-GFP) also redistributed, enabling live-cell confocal imaging which revealed mobile AC9-containing endosomes (Video 1).
evidence: Supported by live-cell imaging data shown in Video 1

claim: AC9 trafficking to endosomes is isoform-specific
source: These results indicate that AC9 traffics dynamically to endosomes containing β2ARs, this trafficking is isoform-specific because AC1 remains in the plasma membrane, and it is regulated because AC9 accumulation in endosomes is increased by β2AR activation.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experimental data comparing AC1 and AC9

claim: AC9 accumulation in endosomes is increased by β2AR activation
source: These results indicate that AC9 traffics dynamically to endosomes containing β2ARs, this trafficking is isoform-specific because AC1 remains in the plasma membrane, and it is regulated because AC9 accumulation in endosomes is increased by β2AR activation.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experimental data

claim: Isoproterenol stimulates selective internalization of Flag-AC9 in the absence of recombinant β2AR overexpression
source: Isoproterenol also stimulated selective internalization of Flag-AC9 in the absence of recombinant β2AR overexpression (Figure 1E and F, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in figures

claim: Alprenolol blocks isoproterenol-stimulated AC9 internalization
source: and this effect was blocked by the β-adrenergic antagonist alprenolol (Figure 1G and H, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in figures

claim: Endogenous β2AR activation is sufficient to stimulate AC9 trafficking
source: These results indicate that endogenous β2AR activation is sufficient to stimulate AC9 trafficking and this is not an off-target drug effect.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experiments with endogenous receptors and antagonist blockade

claim: Endogenous AC9 localizes primarily to the plasma membrane under basal conditions in primary human airway smooth muscle cells
source: Endogenous AC9 immunoreactivity localized in these cells primarily to the plasma membrane under basal conditions, and its localization to internal punctae increased after isoproterenol application (Figure 1I).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1I

claim: Endogenous AC9 localization to internal punctae increases after isoproterenol application in primary human airway smooth muscle cells
source: Endogenous AC9 immunoreactivity localized in these cells primarily to the plasma membrane under basal conditions, and its localization to internal punctae increased after isoproterenol application (Figure 1I).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1I

claim: Internalized β2ARs accumulate in endosomes marked by EEA1
source: Internalized β2ARs accumulate in endosomes marked by Early Endosome Antigen 1 (EEA1) and agonist-dependent activation of Gs by the β2AR occurs on this compartment (Irannejad et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Irannejad et al., 2013

claim: Agonist-dependent activation of Gs by β2AR occurs on EEA1-marked endosomes
source: Internalized β2ARs accumulate in endosomes marked by Early Endosome Antigen 1 (EEA1) and agonist-dependent activation of Gs by the β2AR occurs on this compartment (Irannejad et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Irannejad et al., 2013

claim: Flag-AC9 but not Flag-AC1 localizes to EEA1-marked endosomes
source: We verified isoform-specific localization of Flag-AC9 but not Flag-AC1 to EEA1-marked endosomes by confocal microscopy (Figure 2A and B)
evidence: Supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2A and B

claim: HA-β2AR and Flag-AC9 are enriched in the endosome fraction prepared from isoproterenol-treated cells
source: Coexpressed HA-β2AR and Flag-AC9 were enriched in the endosome fraction prepared from isoproterenol-treated cells, as detected by immunoblot analysis and verified quantitatively across multiple experiments.
evidence: Supported by immunoblot analysis and quantification

claim: HA-β2AR but not Flag-AC1 is enriched in endosome fractions from cells co-expressing HA-β2AR and Flag-AC1
source: In contrast, HA-β2AR but not Flag-AC1 was enriched in parallel isolations from cells co-expressing HA-β2AR and Flag-AC1, with similar levels of overall expression across both cell populations verified in cell lysates (Figure 2C,D, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by immunoblot data shown in figures

claim: The endosome fraction recovers approximately 34% of total cellular EEA1
source: Documenting separation efficiency and fraction purity, the endosome fraction recovered ~34% of total cellular EEA1 but <5% of Golgi, endoplasmic reticulum, or plasma membrane markers (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by biochemical fractionation data shown in supplementary figure

claim: The endosome fraction contains less than 5% of Golgi, endoplasmic reticulum, or plasma membrane markers
source: Documenting separation efficiency and fraction purity, the endosome fraction recovered ~34% of total cellular EEA1 but <5% of Golgi, endoplasmic reticulum, or plasma membrane markers (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by biochemical fractionation data shown in supplementary figure

claim: Isoproterenol produces a marked reduction of Flag-AC9 in the surface-biotinylated fraction
source: Isoproterenol produced a marked reduction of Flag-AC9 in the surface-biotinylated fraction but Flag-AC1 was unchanged, and surface HA-β2AR decreased after isoproterenol application irrespective of whether AC1 or AC9 was coexpressed (Figure 2E,F, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by surface biotinylation data shown in figures

claim: Flag-AC1 in the surface-biotinylated fraction is unchanged after isoproterenol treatment
source: Isoproterenol produced a marked reduction of Flag-AC9 in the surface-biotinylated fraction but Flag-AC1 was unchanged, and surface HA-β2AR decreased after isoproterenol application irrespective of whether AC1 or AC9 was coexpressed (Figure 2E,F, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by surface biotinylation data shown in figures

claim: Surface HA-β2AR decreases after isoproterenol application irrespective of whether AC1 or AC9 is coexpressed
source: Isoproterenol produced a marked reduction of Flag-AC9 in the surface-biotinylated fraction but Flag-AC1 was unchanged, and surface HA-β2AR decreased after isoproterenol application irrespective of whether AC1 or AC9 was coexpressed (Figure 2E,F, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by surface biotinylation data shown in figures

claim: β2AR endocytosis requires dynamin
source: A characteristic property of the conserved, clathrin-dependent pathway mediating β2AR endocytosis is that it also requires dynamin, an endocytic GTPase which can be acutely inhibited by the cell-permeant small molecule DYNGO-4a (Irannejad et al., 2013; Macia et al., 2006; McCluskey et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior studies

claim: DYNGO-4a acutely inhibits dynamin
source: A characteristic property of the conserved, clathrin-dependent pathway mediating β2AR endocytosis is that it also requires dynamin, an endocytic GTPase which can be acutely inhibited by the cell-permeant small molecule DYNGO-4a (Irannejad et al., 2013; Macia et al., 2006; McCluskey et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior studies

claim: DYNGO-4a blocks endosomal accumulation of both Flag-β2AR and AC9-GFP
source: Whereas isoproterenol promoted both Flag-β2AR and AC9-GFP to accumulate in endosomes in the vehicle (0.1% DMSO) control condition (Figure 2G,H, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D), endosomal accumulation of both proteins was blocked in the presence of DYNGO-4a (Figure 2I and J, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in figures

claim: AC9 trafficking to endosomes utilizes a dynamin-dependent membrane pathway
source: These results further support the hypothesis that regulated AC9 trafficking to endosomes utilizes a shared membrane pathway and mechanism relative to regulated endocytosis of the β2AR, and many other GPCRs.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from DYNGO-4a inhibition experiments

claim: AC9 and β2AR traffic independently
source: Despite these similarities, AC9 and β2AR were found to traffic independently.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experimental observations

claim: Brief exposure of cells outside of the tissue culture incubator inhibits AC9 trafficking but β2AR trafficking is resistant to this environmental stress
source: An early clue to this distinction was that brief exposure of cells outside of the tissue culture incubator (see Materials and methods) inhibits AC9 trafficking but β2AR trafficking is resistant to this environmental stress.
evidence: Direct observation from experiments

claim: The V2R is a Gs-coupled GPCR
source: To do so we focused on the vasopressin-2 receptor (V2R), a Gs-coupled GPCR which also undergoes agonist-induced trafficking to early endosomes but is not endogenously expressed in HEK293 cells (Birnbaumer, 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to Birnbaumer, 2000

claim: The V2R undergoes agonist-induced trafficking to early endosomes
source: To do so we focused on the vasopressin-2 receptor (V2R), a Gs-coupled GPCR which also undergoes agonist-induced trafficking to early endosomes but is not endogenously expressed in HEK293 cells (Birnbaumer, 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to Birnbaumer, 2000

claim: The V2R is not endogenously expressed in HEK293 cells
source: To do so we focused on the vasopressin-2 receptor (V2R), a Gs-coupled GPCR which also undergoes agonist-induced trafficking to early endosomes but is not endogenously expressed in HEK293 cells (Birnbaumer, 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to Birnbaumer, 2000

claim: The V2R produces a sustained cAMP response via Gs associated with slow recycling and binding to β-arrestin in endosomes
source: The V2R is of particular interest because this GPCR, unlike the β2AR, has been shown to produce a sustained cAMP response via Gs that is associated with slow recycling and binding to β-arrestin in endosomes (Innamorati et al., 1998, Feinstein et al., 2013; Klein et al., 2001; Oakley et al., 1999; Thomsen et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple prior studies

claim: AVP stimulates redistribution of both Flag-AC9 and HA-V2R to a shared population of endosomes in cells coexpressing HA-V2R
source: However, in cells coexpressing HA-V2R, AVP stimulated the redistribution of both Flag-AC9 and HA-V2R to a shared population of endosomes (Figure 3A,D,E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in figures

claim: AVP-stimulated endocytosis of both Flag-AC9 and HA-V2R was confirmed by surface biotinylation
source: AVP-stimulated endocytosis of both proteins was confirmed by surface biotinylation (Figure 3F,G, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by surface biotinylation data shown in figures

claim: The ability of GPCR activation to promote trafficking of AC9 to endosomes is not unique to the β2AR
source: These results indicate that the ability of GPCR activation to promote trafficking of AC9 to endosomes is not unique to the β2AR. Rather, it appears to be a shared property of GPCRs which activate Gs.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experiments with V2R

claim: The ability to promote AC9 trafficking to endosomes is a shared property of GPCRs which activate Gs
source: These results indicate that the ability of GPCR activation to promote trafficking of AC9 to endosomes is not unique to the β2AR. Rather, it appears to be a shared property of GPCRs which activate Gs.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experiments with multiple Gs-coupled receptors

claim: The MOR transits a similar early endocytic pathway as the β2AR
source: We focused on the µ-opioid receptor (MOP-R or MOR) because this GPCR transits a similar early endocytic pathway as the β2AR (Keith et al., 1998) but activates Gi rather than Gs (Kieffer and Evans, 2009)
evidence: Supported by citation to Keith et al., 1998

claim: The MOR activates Gi rather than Gs
source: We focused on the µ-opioid receptor (MOP-R or MOR) because this GPCR transits a similar early endocytic pathway as the β2AR (Keith et al., 1998) but activates Gi rather than Gs (Kieffer and Evans, 2009)
evidence: Supported by citation to Kieffer and Evans, 2009

claim: Opioid receptors undergo ligand-dependent activation in endosomes
source: and because opioid receptors have been shown explicitly to undergo ligand-dependent activation in endosomes (Stoeber et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Stoeber et al., 2018

claim: DAMGO stimulates HA-MOR to accumulate in endosomes
source: Application of the µ-opioid agonist [D-Ala2, N-MePhe4, Gly-ol]-enkephalin (DAMGO) stimulated transfected HA-MOR to accumulate in endosomes, as shown previously, while Flag-AC9 remained in the plasma membrane (Figure 3B,D,E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in figures

claim: Flag-AC9 remains in the plasma membrane after DAMGO treatment
source: Application of the µ-opioid agonist [D-Ala2, N-MePhe4, Gly-ol]-enkephalin (DAMGO) stimulated transfected HA-MOR to accumulate in endosomes, as shown previously, while Flag-AC9 remained in the plasma membrane (Figure 3B,D,E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in figures

claim: The ability to stimulate AC9 trafficking to endosomes is specific to GPCRs which couple to Gs relative to Gi
source: These results suggest that the ability to stimulate AC9 trafficking to endosomes is a property specific to GPCRs which couple to Gs relative to Gi.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from comparing Gs-coupled and Gi-coupled receptors

claim: HA-V2R-T retains the ability to activate Gs at the plasma membrane
source: This mutant V2R (HA-V2R-T) retains the ability to activate Gs at the plasma membrane but internalizes less efficiently after agonist-induced activation, promotes β-arrestin recruitment to endosomes less strongly and recycles more rapidly (Innamorati et al., 1998; Innamorati et al., 1997; Oakley et al., 1999).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior studies

claim: HA-V2R-T internalizes less efficiently after agonist-induced activation
source: This mutant V2R (HA-V2R-T) retains the ability to activate Gs at the plasma membrane but internalizes less efficiently after agonist-induced activation, promotes β-arrestin recruitment to endosomes less strongly and recycles more rapidly (Innamorati et al., 1998; Innamorati et al., 1997; Oakley et al., 1999).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior studies

claim: HA-V2R-T promotes β-arrestin recruitment to endosomes less strongly than wild-type V2R
source: This mutant V2R (HA-V2R-T) retains the ability to activate Gs at the plasma membrane but internalizes less efficiently after agonist-induced activation, promotes β-arrestin recruitment to endosomes less strongly and recycles more rapidly (Innamorati et al., 1998; Innamorati et al., 1997; Oakley et al., 1999).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior studies

claim: HA-V2R-T recycles more rapidly than wild-type V2R
source: This mutant V2R (HA-V2R-T) retains the ability to activate Gs at the plasma membrane but internalizes less efficiently after agonist-induced activation, promotes β-arrestin recruitment to endosomes less strongly and recycles more rapidly (Innamorati et al., 1998; Innamorati et al., 1997; Oakley et al., 1999).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior studies

claim: Flag-AC9 internalization occurs despite reduced internalization of HA-V2R-T
source: Despite visibly reduced internalization of HA-V2R-T after agonist application (Figure 3C,D,E), Flag-AC9 internalization was still observed (Figure 3C,D,E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1F) and this was confirmed by surface biotinylation (Figure 3F,G).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in figures

claim: Gs-coupled GPCRs share the ability to stimulate AC9 trafficking irrespective of differences in receptor trafficking kinetics or binding to β-arrestin in endosomes
source: These results suggest that Gs-coupled GPCRs share the ability to stimulate AC9 trafficking, irrespective of differences in receptor trafficking kinetics or binding to β-arrestin in endosomes.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experiments with V2R-T mutant

claim: AC9 is relatively insensitive to activation by forskolin
source: While AC9 is relatively insensitive to activation by FSK, other AC isoforms that are major contributors to cAMP production in HEK293 cells (such as AC3 and AC6) are sensitive, making FSK an effective stimulus of overall cAMP elevation (Baldwin et al., 2019; Soto-Velasquez et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior studies

claim: AC3 and AC6 are sensitive to forskolin activation
source: While AC9 is relatively insensitive to activation by FSK, other AC isoforms that are major contributors to cAMP production in HEK293 cells (such as AC3 and AC6) are sensitive, making FSK an effective stimulus of overall cAMP elevation (Baldwin et al., 2019; Soto-Velasquez et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior studies

claim: Forskolin is an effective stimulus of overall cAMP elevation in HEK293 cells
source: While AC9 is relatively insensitive to activation by FSK, other AC isoforms that are major contributors to cAMP production in HEK293 cells (such as AC3 and AC6) are sensitive, making FSK an effective stimulus of overall cAMP elevation (Baldwin et al., 2019; Soto-Velasquez et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior studies

claim: Forskolin does not cause detectable internalization of HA-β2AR
source: FSK did not cause detectable internalization of either HA-β2AR or Flag-AC9 assessed by imaging (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,C,D,I) or surface biotinylation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E,F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in supplementary figures

claim: Forskolin does not cause detectable internalization of Flag-AC9
source: FSK did not cause detectable internalization of either HA-β2AR or Flag-AC9 assessed by imaging (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,C,D,I) or surface biotinylation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E,F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in supplementary figures

claim: Flag-AC1 remains in the plasma membrane in the presence of forskolin
source: Further, as expected, Flag-AC1 remained in the plasma membrane irrespective of the presence of FSK (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B–F,J).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in supplementary figures

claim: IBMX enhances forskolin-induced cAMP elevation in the cytoplasm
source: This was also true in the combined presence of 3-isobutyl-1-methylxanthine (IBMX), a phosphodiesterase inhibitor which enhances FSK-induced cAMP elevation in the cytoplasm (Figure 4—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in supplementary figure

claim: Mutating aspartic acid 442 in AC9 blocks cAMP production
source: We verified that mutating the equivalent residue in AC9 (Flag-AC9-D442A) blocked cAMP production (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in supplementary figure

claim: Regulated trafficking of Flag-AC9-D442A still occurs despite loss of catalytic activity
source: but found that regulated trafficking of Flag-AC9-D442A still occurred (Figure 4—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in supplementary figure

claim: The ability of GPCR-Gs activation to regulate AC9 trafficking is not a consequence of global cytoplasmic cAMP elevation
source: Together, these results indicate that the ability of GPCR-Gs activation to regulate AC9 trafficking is not a consequence of global cytoplasmic cAMP elevation, nor does it require local cAMP production by AC9.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from forskolin and catalytic mutant experiments

claim: AC9 trafficking does not require local cAMP production by AC9
source: Together, these results indicate that the ability of GPCR-Gs activation to regulate AC9 trafficking is not a consequence of global cytoplasmic cAMP elevation, nor does it require local cAMP production by AC9.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from catalytic mutant experiments

claim: HA-Gs-Q227L is constitutively active due to reduced rate of intrinsic GTP hydrolysis
source: We next investigated whether AC9 internalization is regulated by Gs itself, and did so by introducing a point mutation into the alpha subunit (HA-Gs-Q227L) that renders Gs constitutively active by reducing its rate of intrinsic GTP hydrolysis (Masters et al., 1989).
evidence: Supported by citation to Masters et al., 1989

claim: Flag-AC9 localizes to the plasma membrane when coexpressed with wild type HA-Gs in the absence of agonist
source: Flag-AC9 localized to the plasma membrane in the absence of agonist when coexpressed with wild type HA-Gs, but coexpression with activated HA-Gs-Q227L resulted in both proteins localizing to internal punctae (Figure 4A,C,D, Figure 4—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in figures

claim: Coexpression with activated HA-Gs-Q227L results in both Flag-AC9 and HA-Gs-Q227L localizing to internal punctae
source: Flag-AC9 localized to the plasma membrane in the absence of agonist when coexpressed with wild type HA-Gs, but coexpression with activated HA-Gs-Q227L resulted in both proteins localizing to internal punctae (Figure 4A,C,D, Figure 4—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in figures

claim: AC1 remains at the plasma membrane when coexpressed with either HA-Gs or HA-Gs-Q227L
source: This effect was specific to AC9 because AC1 remained at the plasma membrane when coexpressed with either HA-Gs or HA-Gs-Q227L (Figure 4B,C,D, Figure 4—figure supplement 2F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in figures

claim: Both HA-Gs-Q227L and Flag-AC9 accumulate in EEA1-positive endosomes when coexpressed
source: We verified by immunoisolation that both HA-Gs-Q227L and Flag-AC9 accumulate in EEA1-positive endosomes when coexpressed (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A,B)
evidence: Supported by immunoisolation data shown in supplementary figures

claim: Coexpression of HA-Gs-Q227L with Flag-AC1 fails to produce endosome enrichment of either protein
source: whereas coexpression of HA-Gs-Q227L with Flag-AC1 failed to produce endosome enrichment of either protein (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C,D).
evidence: Supported by immunoisolation data shown in supplementary figures

claim: Cholera toxin activation of endogenous Gs results in receptor-independent accumulation of Flag-AC9 in endosomes
source: Independently supporting a discrete regulatory effect of Gs, application of cholera toxin (CTX) to activate the endogenous cellular complement of Gs resulted in receptor-independent accumulation of Flag-AC9, but not Flag-AC1, in endosomes (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in supplementary figure

claim: Cholera toxin does not cause Flag-AC1 to accumulate in endosomes
source: Independently supporting a discrete regulatory effect of Gs, application of cholera toxin (CTX) to activate the endogenous cellular complement of Gs resulted in receptor-independent accumulation of Flag-AC9, but not Flag-AC1, in endosomes (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in supplementary figure

claim: Constitutive activation of Gs produces a degree of endosomal enrichment of AC9 similar to that produced by endogenous β2AR activation with isoproterenol
source: The immunoisolation analysis also indicated that constitutive activation of Gs produced a degree of endosomal enrichment of AC9 similar to that produced in response to endogenous β2AR activation with isoproterenol.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from immunoisolation experiments

claim: Application of isoproterenol to cells coexpressing HA-Gs-Q227L does not detectably increase endosomal enrichment of Gs or AC9
source: Further, application of isoproterenol to cells which coexpress HA-Gs-Q227L did not detectably increase the degree of endosomal enrichment observed for either Gs or AC9 (Figure 4E,F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in figures

claim: Gs activation mediated by endogenous β2ARs is fully sufficient to stimulate AC9 trafficking to endosomes
source: Together, these results suggest that Gs activation mediated by endogenous β2ARs is fully sufficient to stimulate AC9 trafficking to endosomes, without requiring additional effects of upstream receptor activation or downstream cAMP signaling.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experiments with constitutively active Gs

claim: AC9 trafficking does not require additional effects of upstream receptor activation beyond Gs activation
source: Together, these results suggest that Gs activation mediated by endogenous β2ARs is fully sufficient to stimulate AC9 trafficking to endosomes, without requiring additional effects of upstream receptor activation or downstream cAMP signaling.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experiments with constitutively active Gs

claim: AC9-GFP internalization is blocked in GsKO cells while Flag-β2AR still internalizes
source: Flag-β2AR and AC9-EGFP localized to the plasma membrane of GsKO as well as wild type HEK293 cells. However, AC9-GFP internalization was blocked in GsKO cells while Flag-β2AR still internalized.
evidence: Supported by experimental observations in knockout cells

claim: AC9 trafficking is rescued by expression of recombinant HA-Gs in GsKO cells
source: Moreover, AC9 trafficking was rescued by expression of recombinant HA-Gs (Figure 5A-D, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in figures

claim: Gs is necessary for regulated trafficking of AC9 but not β2AR
source: These results indicate that Gs is necessary for regulated trafficking of AC9 but not β2AR.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experiments in GsKO cells

claim: β-arrestins are required for stimulation of β2AR endocytosis by agonists
source: Stimulation of β2AR endocytosis by agonists is known to depend on β-arrestins (Ferguson et al., 1996; Goodman et al., 1996).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior studies

claim: Isoproterenol-stimulated internalization of HA-β2AR is lost in β-arrestin double-knockout cells
source: Isoproterenol-stimulated internalization of HA-β2AR was lost in β-arrestin double-knockout (Arr DKO) cells, as expected, but AC9-EGFP internalization was still observed.
evidence: Supported by experimental observations in knockout cells

claim: AC9-EGFP internalization is still observed in β-arrestin double-knockout cells
source: Isoproterenol-stimulated internalization of HA-β2AR was lost in β-arrestin double-knockout (Arr DKO) cells, as expected, but AC9-EGFP internalization was still observed.
evidence: Supported by experimental observations in knockout cells

claim: Expressing recombinant Arrestin 3 rescues the HA-β2AR trafficking defect in Arr DKO cells without a noticeable change in AC9-EGFP trafficking
source: Further, expressing recombinant Arrestin 3 (β-arrestin-2) rescued the HA-β2AR trafficking defect without a noticeable change in AC9-EGFP trafficking (Figure 5E-H, Figure 5—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in figures

claim: AC9 requires Gs but not β-arrestin for trafficking
source: These results indicate that AC9 and GPCR trafficking are regulated coordinately but through distinct mechanisms– with AC9 requiring Gs but not β-arrestin, and the GPCR requiring β-arrestin but not Gs.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experiments in knockout cells

claim: The GPCR requires β-arrestin but not Gs for trafficking
source: These results indicate that AC9 and GPCR trafficking are regulated coordinately but through distinct mechanisms– with AC9 requiring Gs but not β-arrestin, and the GPCR requiring β-arrestin but not Gs.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experiments in knockout cells

claim: Both AC1 and AC9 are endogenously expressed in HEK293 cells
source: Both AC1 and AC9 are known physiological effectors of β-adrenergic signaling (Sadana and Dessauer, 2009; Small et al., 2003; Tantisira et al., 2005) and both are endogenously expressed in HEK293 cells, despite neither being the primary contributor to global cAMP elevation produced by β2AR activation in this cell type.
evidence: Supported by citations to prior studies

claim: AC1 and AC9 are known physiological effectors of β-adrenergic signaling
source: Both AC1 and AC9 are known physiological effectors of β-adrenergic signaling (Sadana and Dessauer, 2009; Small et al., 2003; Tantisira et al., 2005)
evidence: Supported by citations to prior studies

claim: Neither AC1 nor AC9 is the primary contributor to global cAMP elevation produced by β2AR activation in HEK293 cells
source: Both AC1 and AC9 are known physiological effectors of β-adrenergic signaling (Sadana and Dessauer, 2009; Small et al., 2003; Tantisira et al., 2005) and both are endogenously expressed in HEK293 cells, despite neither being the primary contributor to global cAMP elevation produced by β2AR activation in this cell type.
evidence: Stated as background information

claim: Both AC1 and AC9 make a small but statistically significant contribution to overall cAMP elevation elicited by activation of endogenous β2ARs
source: Nevertheless, analysis by isoform-specific knockdown using siRNA indicated that both AC1 and AC9 make a small but statistically significant contribution to the overall cAMP elevation elicited by activation of endogenous β2ARs.
evidence: Supported by siRNA knockdown experiments

claim: AC1 but not AC9 depletion reduces the forskolin-induced cAMP response
source: AC1 but not AC9 depletion reduced the FSK-induced cAMP response (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), consistent with AC9 being relatively insensitive to stimulation by FSK (Baldwin et al., 2019) and verifying specificity of the knockdown approach.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in supplementary figure

claim: CGP12177 accesses receptors selectively at the plasma membrane
source: We tested this hypothesis using a pharmacological approach based on the ability of the membrane-impermeant β2AR antagonist CGP12177 (CGP) to access receptors selectively at the plasma membrane, whereas the membrane-permeant antagonist alprenolol accesses receptors both at the plasma membrane and endosomes (Staehelin et al., 1983).
evidence: Supported by citation to Staehelin et al., 1983

claim: Alprenolol accesses receptors both at the plasma membrane and endosomes
source: We tested this hypothesis using a pharmacological approach based on the ability of the membrane-impermeant β2AR antagonist CGP12177 (CGP) to access receptors selectively at the plasma membrane, whereas the membrane-permeant antagonist alprenolol accesses receptors both at the plasma membrane and endosomes (Staehelin et al., 1983).
evidence: Supported by citation to Staehelin et al., 1983

claim: This pharmacological approach has been used successfully in previous studies to isolate effects of endosomal activation
source: This approach has been used successfully in previous studies to isolate effects of endosomal activation (Irannejad et al., 2013; Thomsen et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior studies

claim: Isoproterenol promotes recruitment of Nb80-GFP both to the plasma membrane and endosomes
source: Isoproterenol application promoted recruitment of Nb80-GFP both to the plasma membrane and endosomes, and application of excess alprenolol rapidly reversed this activation readout at both locations (Figure 6A, Video 2).
evidence: Supported by live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 6A and Video 2

claim: Alprenolol rapidly reverses Nb80-GFP recruitment at both plasma membrane and endosomes
source: Isoproterenol application promoted recruitment of Nb80-GFP both to the plasma membrane and endosomes, and application of excess alprenolol rapidly reversed this activation readout at both locations (Figure 6A, Video 2).
evidence: Supported by live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 6A and Video 2

claim: CGP reverses Nb80-GFP recruitment only at the plasma membrane but not endosomes
source: Application of CGP, in contrast, reversed Nb80-GFP recruitment only at the plasma membrane but not endosomes (Figure 6B, Video 3).
evidence: Supported by live-cell imaging data shown in Figure 6B and Video 3

claim: Both CGP and alprenolol markedly inhibit isoproterenol-induced cAMP elevation measured at 37°C in living cells
source: Both CGP and alprenolol markedly inhibited the isoproterenol-induced cAMP elevation measured at 37 °C in living cells.
evidence: Supported by cAMP measurements

claim: A large fraction of the overall cAMP elevation elicited by endogenous β2AR activation in HEK293 cells is initiated from the plasma membrane
source: This verifies that a large fraction of the overall cAMP elevation elicited by endogenous β2AR activation in these cells is initiated from the plasma membrane.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from antagonist experiments

claim: Alprenolol produces more pronounced inhibition of cellular cAMP elevation compared to CGP
source: However, we also consistently observed a more pronounced inhibition of cellular cAMP elevation following application of alprenolol compared to CGP (Figure 6C, left set of bars, and Video 4).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C and Video 4

claim: The CGP-resistant 'signal gap' represents the component of cAMP production initiated from endosomes
source: We interpret this difference as a readout of the component of cAMP production initiated from endosomes.
evidence: Interpretation of experimental results

claim: The CGP-resistant signal gap is lost after AC9 knockdown
source: Remarkably, this CGP-resistant 'signal gap' was lost after AC9 knockdown but it remained in cells depleted of AC1 (Figure 6C,D, Figure 6—figure supplement 1C–H).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in figures

claim: The CGP-resistant signal gap remains in cells depleted of AC1
source: Remarkably, this CGP-resistant 'signal gap' was lost after AC9 knockdown but it remained in cells depleted of AC1 (Figure 6C,D, Figure 6—figure supplement 1C–H).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in figures

claim: The increment of isoproterenol-induced cAMP accumulation produced by overexpressing Flag-AC9 in AC3/6 DKO cells is blocked by alprenolol but not CGP
source: The increment of isoproterenol-induced cAMP accumulation produced by overexpressing Flag-AC9 in these cells ('AC9 cAMP response') was blocked by alprenolol but not CGP (Figure 6E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6E

claim: The increment of isoproterenol-induced cAMP accumulation produced by overexpressing Flag-AC1 in AC3/6 DKO cells is blocked by both alprenolol and CGP
source: In contrast, the corresponding increment produced by overexpressing Flag-AC1 ('AC1 cAMP response') was blocked by both alprenolol and CGP (Figure 6F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6F

claim: AC9 selectively contributes to cellular cAMP production initiated by β2AR activation in endosomes using recombinant AC9
source: This verifies that AC9 selectively contributes to cellular cAMP production initiated by β2AR activation in endosomes using recombinant, as well as endogenous AC9.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experiments with recombinant AC9 in AC3/6 DKO cells

claim: AC9 selectively contributes to cellular cAMP production initiated by β2AR activation in endosomes using endogenous AC9
source: This verifies that AC9 selectively contributes to cellular cAMP production initiated by β2AR activation in endosomes using recombinant, as well as endogenous AC9.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from siRNA knockdown experiments

claim: The endocytic network was believed for many years to be silent from the point of view of GPCR-G protein signaling
source: From the point of view of GPCR-G protein signaling, this network was believed for many years to be silent, functioning only in signal termination and longer-term modulation of surface receptor number.
evidence: Historical context from scientific literature

claim: Internalized GPCRs can reacquire the ability to activate G proteins after endocytosis
source: Such homeostatic effects indeed occur, but an accumulating body of evidence supports an expanded view in which internalized GPCRs reacquire the ability to activate G proteins after endocytosis and initiate a second wave of signaling from endomembrane sites (Irannejad et al., 2015; Lohse and Calebiro, 2013; Vilardaga et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior studies

claim: Endosomal signaling depends on the presence of a G protein-regulated effector
source: Endosomal signaling depends on the presence of a G protein-regulated effector, but whether or how effectors localize to relevant internal membrane locations has remained a relatively unexplored frontier.
evidence: Logical inference from signaling requirements

claim: AC9 is widely expressed
source: AC9 is widely expressed (Premont et al., 1996)
evidence: Supported by citation to Premont et al., 1996

claim: AC9 is a physiologically and clinically relevant effector of β2AR-Gs signaling
source: is a physiologically and clinically relevant effector of β2AR-Gs signaling in particular (Small et al., 2003; Sunahara et al., 1996; Tantisira et al., 2005)
evidence: Supported by citations to prior studies

claim: AC9 contributes only a minor fraction to the overall cellular cAMP response elicited by β2AR activation in HEK293 cells
source: We also show that AC9, while contributing only a minor fraction to the overall cellular cAMP response elicited by β2AR activation in this system, is necessary to produce a specific endosome-initiated component of the endogenous β2AR-elicited cAMP response.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experimental data

claim: AC9 is necessary to produce a specific endosome-initiated component of the endogenous β2AR-elicited cAMP response
source: We also show that AC9, while contributing only a minor fraction to the overall cellular cAMP response elicited by β2AR activation in this system, is necessary to produce a specific endosome-initiated component of the endogenous β2AR-elicited cAMP response.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experimental data

claim: AC9 is sufficient to increase cAMP production from endosomes when expressed as a recombinant protein
source: Further, we demonstrate that AC9 is sufficient to increase cAMP production from endosomes when expressed as a recombinant protein.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experimental data

claim: AC1 does not detectably accumulate in endosomes
source: Moreover, we show that AC trafficking is isoform-specific because AC1 does not detectably accumulate in endosomes, nor does AC1 contribute detectably to the endosome-initiated component of cellular cAMP signaling (Figure 6G).
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experimental data

claim: AC1 does not contribute detectably to the endosome-initiated component of cellular cAMP signaling
source: Moreover, we show that AC trafficking is isoform-specific because AC1 does not detectably accumulate in endosomes, nor does AC1 contribute detectably to the endosome-initiated component of cellular cAMP signaling (Figure 6G).
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experimental data

claim: Various isoform-specific protein interactions impact other aspects of AC organization and function
source: We note that various isoform-specific protein interactions which impact other aspects of AC organization and function are already known, with AC9 being a particularly well-studied example (Baldwin et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Baldwin et al., 2019

evidence: Supported by citation to Kriebel et al., 2008

claim: Several other transmembrane AC isoforms have been implicated previously in endomembrane cAMP signaling by mammalian GPCRs
source: We also note that several other transmembrane AC isoforms have been implicated previously in endomembrane cAMP signaling by mammalian GPCRs (Calebiro et al., 2009; Cancino et al., 2014; Ferrandon et al., 2009; Kotowski et al., 2011; Mullershausen et al., 2009; Vilardaga et al., 2014)
evidence: Supported by citations to prior studies

source: and that a distinct AC isoform which lacks any transmembrane domains ('soluble' AC or AC10) has been implicated as well (Inda et al., 2016).

claim: AC9 is not the only isoform to exhibit discrete trafficking behavior
source: Thus we anticipate that AC9 is not the only isoform to exhibit discrete trafficking behavior, and that much remains to be learned along this line.
evidence: Speculation based on existing evidence

claim: The localization and trafficking properties of AC3 and AC6 have yet to be delineated
source: In particular, we note that the localization and trafficking properties of AC3 and AC6– which are major contributors to overall cAMP production stimulated by β2ARs in HEK293 cells (Soto-Velasquez et al., 2018)– have yet to be delineated.
evidence: Statement of knowledge gap

claim: AC5 can form a complex including GPCRs
source: One possible mechanism of AC9 trafficking to GPCR-containing endosomes is by physical association with the receptor or receptor-G protein complex, and there is previous evidence indicating that AC5 can form a complex including GPCRs (Navarro et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Navarro et al., 2018

claim: AC9 traffics independently of β2AR despite trafficking via a similar dynamin-dependent membrane pathway
source: However, our results provide two lines of evidence indicating that AC9 traffics independently, despite trafficking via a similar dynamin-dependent membrane pathway as the β2AR and in a coordinated manner.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experimental data

claim: Activation of Gs is sufficient to promote accumulation of AC9 but not β2AR in endosomes
source: First, activation of Gs is sufficient to promote the accumulation of AC9 but not β2AR in endosomes.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experiments with constitutively active Gs

claim: AC trafficking is likely subject to different modulatory input(s) relative to the trafficking of GPCRs
source: Accordingly, AC trafficking is likely subject to different modulatory input(s) relative to the trafficking of GPCRs.
evidence: Inference from differential regulation

claim: There is significant evidence that cAMP produced internally can mediate different downstream signaling effects relative to cAMP produced from the plasma membrane
source: The physiological significance of isoform-specific AC trafficking also remains to be determined, but we note that there is already significant evidence that cAMP produced internally can mediate different downstream signaling effects relative to cAMP produced from the plasma membrane (O'Banion et al., 2019; Tsvetanova and von Zastrow, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior studies

claim: This is the first study to delineate the dynamic endocytic trafficking of a functionally relevant AC isoform
source: In closing, to our knowledge the present study is the first to delineate the dynamic endocytic trafficking of a functionally relevant AC isoform, and to identify a role of Gs in regulating the trafficking of a defined AC separately from its catalytic activity.
evidence: Authors' assessment of novelty
